tasks.title: Templates and basis plan 0004 T10 wires Ctx.basis
tasks.prTitle: docs(eng-harness): templates and basis plan T10 wires Ctx.basis (B-474)
tasks.notes: Documents-only amendment of packages/eng-harness/docs/plans/0004-templates-and-basis.md (and the engine plan 0001 prose only if a sentence there must point to it). The B.T10 writer (B-164, worktree <worktrees>/b164, read-only for you; handoff note <lead>/reports/b164-writer.md) found that the engine Ctx never exposes `ctx.basis`, which engine spec 0001 section 4.9 and this plan's AC28 need, and that no merged engine task wired it; T10's file list holds tests only, so its workflow test cannot pass. The writer wired it lazily in engine/_ctx_impl.py and engine/_runner.py (36 counted lines; an eager load broke 15 existing tests) in a commit outside the file list. First establish the facts: which task of the engine plan 0001 or of plan 0004 owns the implementation of Ctx.basis (the Ctx types and the basis view came with engine T7; read the plans' files lists and prose and the merged code); whether a not-yet-merged engine task (T13c to T19) already lists it. Then make the smallest correct amendment: if no remaining task owns it, T10 `files` += packages/eng-harness/src/eng_harness/engine/_ctx_impl.py, packages/eng-harness/src/eng_harness/engine/_runner.py and packages/eng-harness/CHANGELOG.md, with a YAML amendment comment (B-474) saying T10 wires Ctx.basis lazily because no engine task did, and the engine plan's shared-file note updated if it lists who edits those two files; keep max_changed_lines at 300 (36 measured). If a remaining engine task does own it, say so in your summary and instead make T10 depend on that task (cross-plan dependency in prose) without adding the files. Keep to this (D-28). The pull request body line is `Plan-Task: none (spec and plan)`.

The task is already written and committed on its branch in the worktree <worktrees>/b164 by an earlier writer who stopped with NEEDS_PLAN_AMENDMENT (the lazy wiring of Ctx.basis in engine/_ctx_impl.py and engine/_runner.py was outside T10's file list; 36 counted lines); amendment B-474 has now merged: read what it decided. If it added those files to T10: merge origin/build/v1 into the branch (no rebase; the engine lane changes the same two engine files, resolve carefully and rerun the engine tests), add the CHANGELOG line, rerun the gate with --skip mutation, recount, update the handoff note. If it instead made T10 depend on an engine task that is not merged yet: return BLOCKED naming that task. Note for the reviewer: the property tests pass at the `test:` commit because they only exercise merged code, while the workflow tests fail there for the right reason; the `test:` commit was amended once before any push to fix lint and type errors. This engine wiring is risk r1 code on the run path: the reviewer checks replay and resume behaviour of the lazy load.
